sections.heading: AC Repair
body: The house is crawling past 80, the vents blow lukewarm air, or the unit outside runs and runs without cooling anything.

Air conditioners fail in a few predictable places: a weak capacitor, a dirty coil, a tired motor, or a refrigerant leak. We find the real cause, explain it plainly and fix it. If an old unit isn't worth repairing, we'll tell you straight and let you decide.

sections.heading: Furnace Repair
body: A furnace that quits rarely says why. It clicks and never lights, runs two minutes and shuts down, or blows cold air while the house gets colder.

The cause is often small: an igniter, a flame sensor, a clogged filter or a failing blower motor. We show you what failed and fix it. A cracked heat exchanger is a safety matter, and we'll tell you plainly if that's what we find.

sections.heading: When a Repair Stops Making Sense
body: When a company that also sells systems tells you yours is finished, it's fair to wonder. So we put the repair next to a new system, and you decide.
If you've paid for two or three repairs in a couple of years and the equipment is old, a new system is usually the cheaper road. Sometimes the honest answer is one more repair.
We install heating and cooling equipment too. A system that is sized and set up badly runs hard and wears out early, so the installation has to be right.

sections.heading: Heat Pumps, Motors and Maintenance
body: We also repair heat pumps and replace blower and condenser motors that have started making noise. Commercial heating and cooling is part of the work too.

A dirty filter, a coil caked with dust and a motor running dry wear a system out a little more each season. A check before the heavy season catches them while they're cheap. We offer maintenance plans, so ask about one when you call.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: The house won't cool below 80, the vent air is lukewarm, the outdoor fan isn't spinning, or the breaker trips every time it starts. Most of the time it's one of a short list of parts.
Ice on the copper line, water around the indoor unit and a system that cycles on and off every few minutes mean turn it off and call. Running a struggling air conditioner makes a small repair bigger.
**Capacitor.** Gives the compressor and fan motor the jolt they need to start. When it weakens, the unit hums and won't run. It's one of the most common and cheapest repairs.
**Dirty coil or clogged filter.** Dust and a choked filter cut airflow until the coil freezes into a block of ice. The fix is cleaning, and finding out why it got that way.
**Low refrigerant.** An air conditioner doesn't use it up, so low means a leak. Adding more without fixing the leak is money that drains away again.
**Fan or compressor motor.** A noisy or slow-spinning motor is a warning. Replacing it early is a far smaller job than waiting for it to fail.

sections.heading: When Your Air Conditioner Quits at a Bad Time

sections.heading: What Usually Stops the Heat
body: The thermostat calls for heat and nothing happens, you hear clicking but the burners never light, or the furnace runs a couple of minutes and shuts off, over and over. Cold rooms, a screaming blower and air that isn't warm are worth a call too.
A furnace goes through several steps before it heats your house, and a failure at any one stops the whole thing. That's why most no-heat calls turn out to be a small part and not a new furnace.
**Igniter.** Lights the burner and wears out with use. A cracked or weak igniter means the furnace tries to start and can't.
**Flame sensor.** This small rod tells the furnace the burner lit. When residue coats it, the furnace shuts down after a few seconds as a safety measure. Cleaning or replacing it is a simple repair.
**Filter and airflow.** A clogged filter makes the furnace overheat and shut itself off. It's the cheapest fix there is, and the reason some furnaces cycle on and off.
**Blower motor.** Moves the warm air through the house. When it fails, the furnace can run and you still get little or no warmth in the rooms.

sections.heading: Repair or New Furnace?
body: Here's a rule you can check. If it's an igniter, a sensor or a motor, repair is the answer. It costs far less than a furnace, and the furnace goes on heating your house.
If the furnace is old, the repairs keep coming, or the heat exchanger has failed, that's when to price a new one. Spending a lot on an old furnace is often money better put toward a new one.

The heat exchanger is the metal chamber that keeps burner exhaust apart from the air you breathe. A crack in it is a safety problem, not an inconvenience. If we find one, you'll hear it straight, with what it means and what your options are. A working carbon monoxide detector on every floor is worth having either way.
We tell you which side of the line you're on. If it's time to replace, we install new furnaces and heating systems too.

sections.heading: Keeping a Furnace Healthy
body: Furnaces fail hardest in the first cold snap, after sitting idle all summer. Dust builds up, parts stiffen and a weak igniter finally gives out.
A check before heating season catches those things while it's still warm outside. We offer maintenance plans, so ask about one when you call. Changing the filter on a schedule helps too.

footer.about: Integrity Heating and Cooling is a family-owned HVAC company in Wichita. Sam and the team repair and replace heating and cooling systems for homes and commercial buildings.
why: We clean up after the job

Your heating and AC pages promise “24/7 Emergency Repair Service.” Your contact page says Monday to Friday, 8 to 5, weekends “at additional cost.” Someone with no heat on a Saturday gets two answers, and that is the call you most need to win.

Your customers already describe the weekend calls you answer. Dayna B.: “Our AC went out called and Sam here in hour on a Saturday morning.” Madison S.: “shoot you straight.” Today those words sit on Google, not on your site.
So the demo tells one story everywhere: your hours, and what to do when the system quits outside them. It opens with HVAC company in Wichita, KS, and gives AC repair and furnace repair a page each.
